frase_gancho.texto: A dry north that preserved textiles, painted vessels, and the memory of desert peoples.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: Northern Mexico is a dry land of great distances. Bands of hunter-gatherers once roamed the desert there, alongside farming peoples who built cities. The dryness of the climate preserved objects that almost always vanish, such as the fibers and textiles of the Candelaria Cave, in Coahuila. In Chihuahua, Paquimé flourished, famous for its painted ceramics and for the raising of macaws. In Alta Vista, in Zacatecas, people made vessels decorated with brightly colored pastes over carved figures.
